questions.question: During Phase 1 of two-phase commit, what message does the coordinator send to all participants?

explanations.a: COMMIT is sent during Phase 2 after the coordinator has made the decision
explanations.b: Correct. PREPARE is the message sent in Phase 1 asking participants if they can commit
explanations.c: While conceptually similar, the standard message name is PREPARE
explanations.d: BEGIN_TRANSACTION would be sent before the commit protocol begins

questions.question: What are the two possible responses a participant can send after receiving a PREPARE message?

explanations.a: While conceptually correct, the standard protocol uses more specific message names
explanations.b: COMMIT and ABORT are decisions sent by the coordinator, not participant responses
explanations.c: Correct. Participants respond with VOTE_COMMIT if they can commit or VOTE_ABORT if they cannot
explanations.d: READY is a state, not a message response in the standard 2PC protocol

questions.question: In the simulation, what happens to participants after they vote YES in Phase 1?

answers.b: They enter the PREPARED state and hold locks
answers.c: They release all resources and wait
answers.d: They send confirmation to other participants

explanations.a: Participants wait for the global decision before committing
explanations.b: Correct. After voting YES, participants enter PREPARED state and continue holding their locks until Phase 2
explanations.c: Resources and locks must be held until the final decision is made
explanations.d: Participants only communicate with the coordinator, not with each other

questions.question: What determines whether the coordinator sends GLOBAL_COMMIT or GLOBAL_ABORT in Phase 2?

answers.a: The coordinator's own readiness to commit
answers.b: Whether the majority of participants voted to commit
answers.c: Whether ALL participants voted to commit
answers.d: The priority level of the transaction

explanations.a: The coordinator's decision is based solely on participant votes
explanations.b: 2PC requires unanimity, not majority - even one abort vote causes global abort
explanations.c: Correct. Only if ALL participants vote to commit will the coordinator send GLOBAL_COMMIT; any abort vote results in GLOBAL_ABORT
explanations.d: Transaction priority is not a factor in the 2PC decision process

questions.question: According to the protocol phases, when do participants release their locks?

answers.b: When they receive the global decision in Phase 2
answers.c: After executing the commit or abort and sending ACK
answers.d: Only when the entire transaction is complete across all nodes

explanations.a: Locks must be held through Phase 1 to ensure transaction integrity
explanations.b: Receiving the decision is not sufficient; the participant must also execute it
explanations.c: Correct. Participants release locks after executing the commit/abort decision and sending acknowledgment
explanations.d: Each participant can release locks after completing its own commit/abort execution

questions.question: In the failure scenario simulation, what causes a transaction to be aborted during Phase 1?

answers.b: A participant failing before responding to PREPARE
answers.c: The coordinator taking too long to make a decision

explanations.a: Network delays might cause timeouts but don't directly cause abort decisions
explanations.b: Correct. If a participant fails during Phase 1, the coordinator will timeout waiting for its vote and decide to abort
explanations.c: The coordinator's decision speed doesn't cause abortion; it's based on participant responses
explanations.d: Lock contention is handled at the participant level and might cause a participant to vote abort

questions.question: What is the consequence of coordinator failure during Phase 2 (after making the decision)?

answers.a: All participants automatically abort the transaction
answers.b: Participants who voted commit remain blocked in PREPARED state
answers.c: The transaction outcome depends on which participants received the decision
answers.d: A new coordinator must be elected to complete the transaction

explanations.a: Participants cannot unilaterally abort after voting commit - this would violate atomicity
explanations.b: Participants who received the decision can proceed; others remain blocked waiting
explanations.c: Correct. Some participants may have received COMMIT/ABORT while others are still waiting, creating inconsistency until recovery
explanations.d: While coordinator failover is possible, the immediate consequence is the inconsistent state

questions.question: In the context of recovery, what must a participant do if it finds 'READY' logged in its durable storage after restart?

answers.a: Assume the transaction was aborted and roll back
answers.b: Assume the transaction was committed and apply changes
answers.c: Contact the coordinator to learn the final decision
answers.d: Wait for other participants to contact it with the decision

explanations.a: The participant cannot assume abort - this might violate atomicity if others committed
explanations.b: The participant cannot assume commit without confirmation from the coordinator
explanations.c: Correct. A 'READY' state means the participant voted to commit but doesn't know the final decision, so it must contact the coordinator
explanations.d: Other participants don't know the global decision either; only the coordinator does

questions.question: Why is two-phase commit considered a 'blocking' protocol?

answers.a: It blocks other transactions from starting while one is in progress
answers.b: Network messages can be blocked by failures or partitions
answers.c: Participants in READY state cannot proceed without coordinator contact
answers.d: The coordinator blocks until all participants respond

explanations.a: This describes a concurrency limitation, not the inherent blocking property of 2PC
explanations.b: While network issues can occur, this isn't what makes 2PC fundamentally blocking
explanations.c: Correct. Participants who voted commit and entered READY state cannot unilaterally abort - they are blocked waiting for the coordinator's decision
explanations.d: Coordinator blocking on responses is normal protocol behavior, not the problematic blocking property
